h1: What a local SEO agency does differently
metaTitle: What Is a Local SEO Agency? What It Does
metaDescription: What is a local SEO agency? One that competes for the Google map pack, not page one. The different work, the different metrics, and what it costs in India.
answer: A local SEO agency competes for the Google map pack — the three business listings that sit above the blue links — rather than for national rankings. The work is Google Business Profile management, citation cleanup, review generation and location pages. It's usually cheaper than national SEO, because your competitive set is your neighbourhood, not the country.
takeaways: Local SEO is scored on a **different board**. Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence — and you cannot change distance.
For a single-location business, most of a national SEO retainer is spent on work that will never influence the map pack.
In India the citation problem is worse than the playbooks admit, because addresses are landmark-based and city names have two spellings each.
Reviews are the one lever an agency can't pull for you. They can build the system; your staff still has to ask.

sections.h2: Two different scoreboards on the same results page
body: Search "dentist near me" and you get two competitions stacked on one page. At the top, a map with three business listings. Below it, the ordinary blue links. They're ranked by different signals, won by different work, and a lot of money gets wasted by agencies optimising for the second while the client cares about the first.

Google's own documentation is clear that local results are ranked on three things: relevance, distance and prominence. That third word is where an agency earns its fee. The second one is where physics beats budget.

callout.title: Most local businesses need both, weighted
callout.body: The map pack brings the phone calls; the website closes them and catches the searches without local intent. A sane local engagement spends most of its hours on the profile and the local signals, and just enough on the site to make it fast, correct and convincing.

sections.h2: What a local SEO agency actually does each month
body: Strip out the jargon and the monthly work is narrower than national SEO and considerably more repetitive. That's not a criticism — repetition is what wins here.

bullets: Primary and secondary category selection. The single highest-impact setting on the whole profile, and the one most often left on whatever was picked in 2019.
Services, products, attributes, opening hours including festival closures, and holiday hours that don't go stale.
Posts, photos and Q&A. Real photos with real dates, not stock. Seeding and answering the questions customers actually ask.
Monitoring for unauthorised edits. Anyone can suggest a change to your listing, and competitors sometimes do.

subs.h3: Local landing pages that aren't duplicates
bullets: One genuinely distinct page per location — real address, real staff, real parking directions, real photos of that branch.
The failure mode: 40 pages identical except for a swapped city name. Google classifies that as scaled content, and it stopped working years ago.
Embedded map, local schema, and a phone number that's clickable on mobile without pinch-zooming.
Auditing and correcting listings across the directories that matter in your city and sector.
A review system: the ask, the timing, the follow-up and the response process.
Links from genuinely local sources — trade associations, local news, sponsorships, supplier and partner sites. Far more achievable than national press, and they count for prominence.

sections.h2: The proximity ceiling nobody puts in the proposal
body: Here's the uncomfortable structural fact about local SEO. Distance is a ranking factor you cannot optimise. If your clinic is in Indiranagar, a searcher in Whitefield is unlikely to see you in the map pack no matter how good your profile is — Google is answering "near me" literally, and it should.

This has a hard consequence for budgeting. Your realistic catchment is a radius, not a city. In dense areas that radius can be a couple of kilometres; in sparse ones it stretches, because there's nothing closer to show. It also varies by category — people will travel further for a specialist surgeon than for a haircut, and Google's results reflect that.

So before you buy a retainer aimed at "ranking in Mumbai", work out how many people live inside your actual radius, how many of them search for your category in a month, and what share of that you could plausibly win. Sometimes the honest answer is that the ceiling on the channel is lower than the retainer, and the money belongs in paid social or a second location instead.

The exception is anything genuinely destination-based — a specialist hospital, a wedding venue, a showroom people plan a trip to. There, broader local and organic work both make sense, and the split shifts. We lay out the full trade-off in [local SEO vs national SEO](/compare/local-seo-vs-national-seo).

callout.title: The rank tracker lies to you here
callout.body: Local rankings are personalised by the searcher's location, so checking your own phone tells you almost nothing. Any agency reporting one flat "rank 2 for dentist in Pune" is either using a single arbitrary coordinate or hoping you don't ask. Ask for a grid — rankings sampled across multiple points around your address — because that's what your catchment actually looks like.

sections.h2: Citations and NAP consistency, the Indian version
body: NAP means name, address and phone number, and the rule is that they should match everywhere they appear. It sounds like clerical work. In India it's genuinely difficult, and it's where a competent local agency earns a surprising share of its fee.
The reasons are specific to the market.
bullets: **Addresses are landmark-based.** "Opp. HDFC Bank, above Sagar Ratna, 2nd Cross" is how customers find you and how directories store it. Google prefers structured, consistent formatting. Both have to be true at once.
**City names have two official spellings.** Bangalore and Bengaluru. Gurgaon and Gurugram. Trivandrum and Thiruvananthapuram. Your listings are probably split across both, and so are your reviews.
**Locality names nest ambiguously.** Sector, block, phase, colony, nagar and layout are used inconsistently between directories, and PIN codes cover areas people don't think of as one place.

**The directory set is different.** Justdial, Sulekha and IndiaMART matter here in ways they don't elsewhere, and sector-specific platforms often matter more than general ones — Practo for clinics, Zomato and Swiggy for restaurants, 99acres and MagicBricks for property, Urban Company for home services.

**Phone numbers multiply.** A landline, a mobile, a WhatsApp Business number and an IVR number from an old campaign, spread across six listings. Pick one, standardise the format, and use call tracking that preserves the displayed number rather than replacing it.

callout.title: Do this before you buy anything
callout.body: Search your business name in Google and open the first three directory listings. If the address format differs, the phone number differs, or there's a branch you closed in 2022 still listed, you have citation work to do — and it's cheap, one-time work that any agency should quote separately rather than bundle into a permanent retainer.

sections.h2: Reviews: the lever your agency can't pull
body: Review volume, rating and recency all feed prominence, and prominence is the part of the local ranking you can actually influence. Every local SEO agency knows this. Very few will tell you that the hard part happens on your side of the counter.

An agency can build the system — the QR code at the billing desk, the WhatsApp follow-up two hours after the appointment, the review link that skips three clicks, the response templates, the monthly report on what people complained about. It cannot make your receptionist ask.

The pattern we see repeatedly: businesses that get 30 reviews in the first month of a push and then nothing, because the person who was asking left. Steady beats spiky here too. Four honest reviews a month, indefinitely, outperforms a burst.

Two things worth stating plainly. Buying reviews violates Google's policies and the fake ones are increasingly removed in sweeps that take your rating down with them. And responding to negative reviews matters more than most owners think — not for the algorithm, but because the next customer reads the response and decides whether you're the kind of business that argues with a 2-star.

sections.h2: When a local agency is the cheaper, better buy
body: A national SEO retainer includes things a single-location business will never benefit from: content programmes aimed at nationwide informational queries, link campaigns targeting authority you don't need, and technical work sized for a site with thousands of URLs. You pay for all of it.

For a single clinic, salon, restaurant, gym or law practice, the sensible engagement is much narrower — profile, citations, reviews, a handful of genuinely good pages, and local links. Less labour, so it should cost less. In India, single-location local work commonly sits between ₹15,000 and ₹50,000 a month, and the spread reflects how many locations, how competitive the category, and whether the website needs rebuilding.

The line moves when you add locations. Somewhere around five to ten branches the work stops being local hygiene and becomes a real content and technical programme — location page architecture, internal linking, duplicate management, bulk profile administration — and a full retainer starts making sense again.

Our own SEO starts at ₹75,000/month, with smaller sites from ₹40,000. For a genuinely single-location business, we'll usually tell you the ₹40,000 tier is the right one or that you don't need us at all yet — [how to do local SEO](/answers/how-to-do-local-seo) covers what you can do without hiring anyone. When we do take the work, the guarantee is the same: we freeze your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search on day one, and if we haven't beaten that in 90 days we keep working free until we do. Never a promised map position — nobody can control that, least of all for a searcher standing 8 km away.

callout.title: The multi-location trap
callout.body: If you're quoted a per-location monthly fee, check what's actually delivered per location. Twenty branches at ₹8,000 each is ₹1,60,000/month, and the work is often one bulk listings update plus a report. Per-location pricing suits the agency's spreadsheet, not your results. See [what local SEO costs](/cost/local-seo-cost).

faqs.q: What's the difference between a local SEO agency and a regular SEO agency?
faqs.a: A local agency works primarily on your Google Business Profile, citations, reviews and location pages to win the map pack. A regular SEO agency works on the website to win organic blue links nationally. The signals differ, the timelines differ, and the local version is usually cheaper because there's less of it.

faqs.q: How much does a local SEO agency cost in India?
faqs.a: Single-location work commonly runs ₹15,000–₹50,000 a month, depending on category competitiveness and whether the site needs rebuilding. Multi-location programmes cost more because the content and technical work scales with branches. Our SEO starts at ₹75,000/month, with smaller sites from ₹40,000.

faqs.q: How long does local SEO take to work?
faqs.a: Faster than national SEO. Profile and category fixes can shift map pack visibility within days to a few weeks, and review and citation work usually shows up in 4–8 weeks. Competitive urban categories like dentistry or real estate take longer because everyone nearby is doing the same work.

faqs.q: Do I need a website if I have a Google Business Profile?
faqs.a: You'll rank in the map pack without one, but you'll convert worse and win fewer non-local searches. The profile brings the click; the site answers the questions that decide the call. For most local businesses a small, fast, honest site is a cheap addition, not an alternative.

faqs.q: Can a local SEO agency guarantee I'll be in the map pack?
faqs.a: No, and anyone who does is ignoring distance. Map pack results change with the searcher's location, so the same business can be first for someone across the road and invisible two kilometres away. A guarantee tied to your own lead baseline is honest; a guaranteed position isn't.

faqs.q: Are directory citations still worth doing in 2026?
faqs.a: As a one-time cleanup, yes — inconsistent listings genuinely confuse things and the fix is cheap. As an ongoing monthly line item paying for 50 new submissions a month, no. Once your core listings are correct and consistent, the returns drop off sharply.
